I wouldn't complicate this to have multiple states, just always advertise the best source address for the current default gateway. If it's missing, fall back to the older behavior as that either means no real default is available or the CNBMC is old.
Done

If you are going to do this you need to keep track of the metrics and srcs and maintain a dict to keep track of them as they change. You need to pick the best one to make a source route for regardless of the order they are discovered / go away. That way you can fall back to the NCSI port here when the front panel goes away. We can't just ignore sending the NCSI address because we should send the right ones. If we have a default gateway, we should send the route.
I think only this hybrid oob ip will use this special /124 address, all other addresses will be unaffected by this so there is no need to make this channel universal for all types of addresses?
Done. Now just sending the highest metric route
I think you need to restore this and delete the dups below. None of the below logic should act on the 700 metric route.
No 700 is actually important, we should pick whatever the highest priority in main table including the 700 one.
Done

I think your comment is backwards here. But I think the logic is kinda misleading. It doesn't matter if you are a tray, technically in a zebrafish style tray, the tray could provide outbound access for the CN BMC if the CN BMC links go down.
We don't want to let tray provide an alternative path for CN BMC. There can be multiple tray BMCs so that it can be multiple primary ips. Just blocking the path is cleaner IMHO.
Done
I don't think you want this here, it still will happen in the above src calculation no?
Which one are you refering to? This is the only place updating the /124 RA route.
Done
Parse this once before the if stmt. Also use local variables all around here.
will do
Done

I don't think this is guaranteed, you can delete it for other reasons (like networkd reloading) and still have the expires value be positive iirc.

In theory the proper way to handle it is to use the ip monitoring defer statement, since it will defer the action until after the batched monitored actions. You call `gbmc_ip_monitor_defer` here and then have a handler for $change == defer above. You would only update things if the value of $primary_ip_from_br differed from the set value.

I think it does not matter whether it is removed correctly or not, we mainly rely on new coming routes to refresh the route and most of the time the expire triggers nothing. even there is a reload and it deletes an unexpired route, the RA route will still refresh it correctly.
Done
Why is this not just part of the primary route updating / setting? It should always reflect the same value.
Done
